row.title: Treat any untoward medical occurrence with drug use as an adverse event for IND safety reporting, related or not
row.statement: For IND safety reporting under 21 CFR 312.32, the sponsor must treat as an adverse event any untoward medical occurrence associated with the use of a drug in humans, whether or not it is considered drug related.

row.title: Classify an event as life-threatening only if it placed the subject at immediate risk of death
row.statement: When assessing events for IND safety reporting, the sponsor must classify an adverse event or suspected adverse reaction as life-threatening if, in the view of either the investigator or the sponsor, its occurrence places the patient or subject at immediate risk of death; an event that might have caused death only had it occurred in a more severe form is not life-threatening.

row.title: Classify an event as serious when it results in death, a life-threatening event, hospitalisation, disability or birth defect
row.statement: When assessing events for IND safety reporting, the sponsor must classify an adverse event or suspected adverse reaction as serious if, in the view of either the investigator or the sponsor, it results in death, a life-threatening adverse event, inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization, a persistent or significant incapacity or substantial disruption of the ability to conduct normal life functions, or a congenital anomaly/birth defect.

row.title: Treat an adverse event as a suspected adverse reaction when there is a reasonable possibility the drug caused it
row.statement: For IND safety reporting, the sponsor must treat as a suspected adverse reaction any adverse event for which there is a reasonable possibility that the drug caused it, meaning there is evidence to suggest a causal relationship between the drug and the adverse event.

row.title: Treat class effects or pharmacologically anticipated events not specifically listed for the drug as unexpected
row.statement: For IND safety reporting, the sponsor must also treat as unexpected adverse events or suspected adverse reactions that the investigator brochure mentions as occurring with a class of drugs or as anticipated from the drug's pharmacological properties, but not specifically as occurring with the particular drug under investigation.
